<STRUCT_0001>
In this chapter we discuss Artin's axioms for the representability of
functors by algebraic spaces. As references we suggest the papers
<REF_0001>, <REF_0002>, <REF_0003>.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Some of the notation, conventions, and terminology in this chapter is awkward
and may seem backwards to the more experienced reader. This is intentional.
Please see Quot, Section <REF_0004> for an
explanation.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
Let <MATH_0001> be a locally Noetherian base scheme. Let
<MATH_0002>

over a field <MATH_0005> of finite type over <MATH_0006>. Throughout this chapter an important
role is played by the predeformation category
(see Formal Deformation Theory,
Definition <REF_0005>)

associated to <MATH_0007> over <MATH_0008>. We introduce the Rim-Schlessinger condition (RS)
for <MATH_0009> and show it guarantees that
<MATH_0010> is a deformation category, i.e.,
<MATH_0011> satisfies (RS) itself.
We discuss how <MATH_0012>
changes if one replaces <MATH_0013> by a finite extension
and we discuss tangent spaces.

<STRUCT_0006><STRUCT_0007>
Next, we discuss formal objects <MATH_0014> of <MATH_0015> which are

A formal object is called effective when there is an object of

A formal object of <MATH_0025> is called versal if it gives rise to a
versal formal object of <MATH_0026>.
Finally, given a finite type <MATH_0027>-scheme <MATH_0028>, an object <MATH_0029>
of <MATH_0030> over <MATH_0031>, and a closed point <MATH_0032> we say
<MATH_0033> is versal at <MATH_0034> if the induced formal object over the complete

Having worked through this material we can state Artin's celebrated

<STRUCT_0020><STRUCT_0021>
Here is a rough outline of the proof of Artin's theorem.
First we show that there are plenty of versal formal objects
using (RS) and the finite dimensionality of tangent and aut spaces, see
for example Formal Deformation Theory, Lemma
<REF_0010>.
These formal objects are effective by assumption.
Effective formal objects can be ``approximated'' by objects <MATH_0047> over
finite type <MATH_0048>-schemes <MATH_0049>, see Lemma <REF_0011>.
This approximation uses the local rings of <MATH_0050> are G-rings and
that <MATH_0051> is limit preserving; it is perhaps the most difficult
part of the proof relying as it does on general N<ACCENT_0002>ron desingularization to
approximate formal solutions of algebraic equations over a Noetherian local
G-ring by solutions in the henselization.
Next openness of versality implies we may (after shrinking <MATH_0052>)
assume <MATH_0053> is versal at every closed point of <MATH_0054>.
Having done all of this we show that <MATH_0055>
is a smooth morphism. Taking sufficiently many <MATH_0056>
we show that we obtain a ``smooth atlas'' for <MATH_0057> which shows
that <MATH_0058> is an algebraic stack.

<STRUCT_0022><STRUCT_0023>
In checking Artin's axioms for a given category <MATH_0059> fibred
in groupoids, the most difficult step is often to verify openness
of versality. For the discussion that follows, assume that <MATH_0060>
already satisfies the other conditions listed above.
In this chapter we offer two methods that will allow the reader
to prove <MATH_0061> satisfies openness of versality:
<STRUCT_0024>
<STRUCT_0025> The first is to assume a stronger Rim-Schlessinger
condition, called (RS*) and to assume a stronger version of
formal effectiveness, essentially requiring objects over
inverse systems of thickenings to be effective. It turns out
that under these assumptions, openness of versality comes for
free, see Lemma <REF_0012>.
Please observe that here we are using in an essential manner
that <MATH_0062> is defined on that category of all schemes
over <MATH_0063>, not just the category of Noetherian schemes!
<STRUCT_0026> The second, following Artin, is to require <MATH_0064>
to come equipped with an obstruction theory. If said obstruction
theory ``commutes with products'' in a suitable sense, then
<MATH_0065> satisfies openness of versality, see
Lemma <REF_0013>.
<STRUCT_0027>
Obstruction theories can be axiomatized in many different ways
and indeed many variants (often adapted to specific moduli stacks)
can be found in the literature. We explain a variant using the derived category
(which often arises naturally from deformation theory computations
done in the literature) in Lemma <REF_0014>.
